title: MathCursor — Getting started
intro: For each prompt, try it out in the box on the right. Type, look, try again. Whitespace matters in MathCursor: it separates what is grouped.

sections.title: How the popup works
sections.intro: As soon as MathCursor recognises a notation, a small grey popup appears above the caret with the main conversion (preselected) and the possible alternatives. `Enter` accepts the selected suggestion. `Down arrow` then `Enter` picks an alternative. `Esc` dismisses the popup without inserting anything. If nothing appears (because you're in silent mode, or MathCursor didn't catch your intent), `Ctrl + Space` forces the popup.

sections.title: Fractions
sections.intro: Type the `/` operator. Numerator and denominator are built automatically.

items.instruction: Plain fraction — type `1/x`.
With a space, the fraction stops at `/`. Type `1/x +1` (space before `+`).
Without a space, MathCursor keeps standard math precedence but offers the extension in the popup. Type `1/x+1` (no space).
Two letters stuck together count as a single unit. Type `AB/BC` — the fraction forms. The popup also offers a vector variant for `BC` (the rightmost match, closest to the caret).

sections.title: Superscripts & subscripts
sections.intro: Type a digit after a letter: MathCursor proposes the superscript; the popup proposes the subscript. To force either explicitly, use `^` (superscript) or `_` (subscript).

items.instruction: Type `x2`. MathCursor proposes `x²`; the popup proposes `x₂`.
To force the superscript, type `x^2`. No popup — explicit choice.
Simple subscript — type `u_n`.
Extended subscript — type `u_n+1` (no space). Default = `uₙ + 1`, popup = `uₙ₊₁`.
Same idea for superscripts — type `x^a+b` (no space).

sections.title: Vectors
sections.intro: Two adjacent capital letters are ambiguous (vector, segment, length). MathCursor offers the options in the popup; you pick.

items.instruction: Explicit `vec` notation — type `vec u`.
Type `AB`. The popup offers `→AB` (vector), `(AB)` (line), `[AB]` (segment).
Column coordinates — type `u (1 2)` (spaces between values).
Row coordinates — type `u(1, 2)` (commas).

sections.title: Canonical sets
sections.intro: The sets `R`, `N`, `Z`, `Q`, `C` show a popup to switch between the plain letter and the set form `ℝ`, `ℕ`, etc. Prefix with `bb` to force the set rendering.

items.instruction: Type `bbR` to force `ℝ`.
Type `bbR*` for `ℝ*`.
Type `forall x in bbR` for `∀x ∈ ℝ`.

sections.title: Intervals
sections.intro: Type the brackets directly, open or closed. Combine with `union`, `inter`, or the contextual `U`.

items.instruction: Closed interval — type `[0,1]`.
Open on the right — type `[0,1[`.
Union — type `[0,1] U [3,5]` (`U` is recognised between intervals).
Intersection — type `[0,1] inter [1,2]`.

sections.title: Roots & functions
sections.intro: Keywords in English. No need for parentheses if the argument is short; add them for compound expressions.

items.instruction: Square root — type `sqrt x`.
Short cosine — type `cos x`.
Compound cosine — type `cos(x+y)`.
Fraction of functions — type `frac sin x x` for `sin(x)/x`.

sections.title: Sums, limits, integrals
sections.intro: Keyword followed by arguments separated by spaces. No `_{...}^{...}` to type — it's positional.

items.instruction: Limit — type `lim x 0 f(x)` for `lim x→0 f(x)`.
Sum — type `sum k 1 n k` for `Σ k=1..n k`.
Integral — type `int 0 1 x`.
With a compound expression — type `sum k 1 n f(k) + g(k)` (spaces around `+`).

sections.title: The disambiguation popup
sections.intro: When several readings are possible, MathCursor picks the most likely one and offers the others in the popup. You can switch at any time with Down arrow + Enter.

items.instruction: Decimal vs product — type `3.4`. Default = `3·4` (product), popup = `3,4` (decimal).
Dot product — type `u*v`. Default = `u·v`, popup = `→u · →v`.
Call vs vector — type `f(1, 2)`. Default = call `f(1,2)`, popup = `→f(1 ; 2)`.
Two-point angle — type `^AB`. The 3rd point is pending.
